sources.scope_note: The Presidency's consolidated legislation page for the decree, captured by the Internet Archive on 24 June 2012; the page states that it does not replace the DOU publication of 8 January 1990. claims.text: Decree No. 98.797 of 5 January 1990, issued by the President of the Republic under Article 84(IV) of the Constitution to revise the values fixed in Decree-Law No. 2.300 of 1986, is dated Brasília 5 January 1990 and signed José Sarney (countersigned João Batista de Abreu); the page notes publication in the DOU of 8 January 1990.

locator.item: heading; preamble 'O PRESIDENTE DA REPÚBLICA'; signature block; note 'Este texto não substitui o publicado no D.O.U. de 8.1.1990'

claims.uncertainty: A signed act attests that Sarney exercised the office on the act's date; it is not a start, an end or a term. The Planalto page is the Presidency's consolidated legislation text, which states that it does not replace the DOU publication. It is the earliest 1990 attestation pinned to a byte-stable response, not the earliest that exists: Decree No. 98.785 of 4 January 1990 (read live) and a Presidency Library speech listed for 4 January 1990 are known, but the archived captures of the decree are bot-check pages and neither is pinned.

sources.scope_note: Photograph (JPEG, 1420x1969) of the diploma in the TSE digital library, item bdtse/1942 (http://bibliotecadigital.tse.jus.br/handle/bdtse/1942); a static bitstream whose ETag equals the MD5 of the bytes (Last-Modified 12 February 2016). The item's catalogue record (https://bibliotecadigital.tse.jus.br/server/api/core/items/25131fb9-9676-49e2-81fc-fadd43f3a79a; 6,656 bytes, SHA-256 5f2621f2e0ff3a11b418902655abc43dafafaaa7f2f451b8537dcf1b7156ac52, stable across two downloads) describes the pictured signed exemplar as an object of the TSE's memory collection acquired by collection ('Coleta') in 1995 and lists unsigned photographic models among related material: it is the TSE's collection exemplar, and nothing here shows it is the exemplar handed to Collor. published_date is the date printed on the diploma.

claims.text: The Superior Electoral Court's diploma, dated Brasília 30 December 1989 and signed by its President, Minister Francisco Rezek, and the other ministers, certifies that Fernando Collor was elected President of the Republic and qualifies him for investiture in the office before the National Congress on 15 March 1990 under the Constitution.

locator.lines: dating line 'Brasília, aos 30 de dezembro de 1989'; body text

claims.uncertainty: The diploma's issue date; the ceremony itself is dated by the TSE catalogue and the 1990 posse record. The investiture day printed on the diploma is prospective and is not a start. The pictured signed exemplar is the TSE's own collection object (catalogue record bdtse/1942: acquired by collection in 1995), not shown to be the exemplar handed to Collor; the printed date is unaffected. Never a holder date.

claims.text: The diploma states that the will of the Brazilian people was expressed at the ballots of 15 November and 17 December 1989, by which Fernando Collor was elected President of the Republic.
claims.uncertainty: Election observation dated by the second (deciding) ballot; the first ballot of 15 November 1989 is in the text. Not a start of office. Never a holder date.

sources.title: Diário do Congresso Nacional nº 8, 16 March 1990: minutes of the 8th joint session of 15 March 1990 (posse)
sources.publisher: Congresso Nacional (printed by the Senado Federal)
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, seals, coats of arms, signatures, diploma images or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: Scanned Diário do Congresso Nacional issue from the Senate's diary store (viewer https://legis.senado.leg.br/diarios/ver/14789).

claims.text: At the solemn joint session of 15 March 1990, after the constitutional oath, the President of the National Congress, Senator Nelson Carneiro, declared Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested ('empossados') as President and Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Nelson Carneiro) - Declaro empossados ...

claims.uncertainty: Posse record with an explicit mandate start of 15 March 1990 (the basis for Collor's from). The Vice-President's posse is the same act and is outside this role.

claims.text: The termo de posse read and signed at the session records that at 10:00 on 15 March 1990, before the National Congress in joint session in the Chamber's plenary, Collor and Itamar Franco were solemnly invested under Article 78 of the Constitution in the offices of President and Vice-President for the period from 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995, and took the prescribed oath.

locator.item: Termo de posse, first paragraph

claims.uncertainty: Same event as the declaration, recorded in the signed termo; the termo's clock time is not relied on.

claims.text: In his address to the joint session of 15 March 1990 Fernando Collor brings to the Legislative Power, before which, following the Constitution, he 'acabo de assumir a Presidência da República' (has just assumed the Presidency of the Republic), his esteem and homage.

locator.item: Collor's address: 'Venho trazer ao Poder Legislativo, ante o qual, seguindo o preceito da Constituição, acabo de assumir a Presidência da República'

claims.uncertainty: The holder's own statement in the Congress record, dated by the session; it supports the declaration and the termo (the basis for from) and gives no clock time. Found by the independent check.

claims.text: The same termo recites that they had been elected in the second round on 17 December of the previous year and certified ('diplomados') by the Superior Electoral Court on 30 December of that year.

locator.item: Termo de posse, 'diplomados, pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, a trinta de dezembro do mesmo ano'

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital of the TSE act, not the TSE's own record; agrees with the diploma. Never a holder date.

claims.text: The session was opened to give posse to the President and Vice-President elected in the second round on 17 December 1989 and certified by the TSE for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: opening statement of the President of Congress

claims.uncertainty: Election recital; never a start or a holder date.

claims.text: Opening the solemn joint session of 15 March 1990, the President of Congress, Senator Nelson Carneiro, stated that it was convened to give posse to the President and Vice-President of the Republic elected in the second round on 17 December 1989 and certified ('diplomados') by the Superior Electoral Court for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995, naming Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Nelson Carneiro) - Declaro aberta a sessão solene ... destinada a dar posse ao Presidente e Vice-Presidente da República

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital of the second-round election; never a start or a holder date. The same passage is already recorded for the President as br_collor_second_round_recited_19891217.

claims.text: After the session resumed (suspended 9:43-9:46), the President and the Vice-President-elect were seated at the Mesa, the Vice-President to the left of the President of the Senate, and both took the constitutional oath ('Prometo manter, defender e cumprir a Constituição ...') before the joint session.

locator.item: 'Os Srs. Presidente e Vice-Presidente da República irão prestar o compromisso constitucional'; the oath text continues on printed page 302

claims.uncertainty: A distinct event recorded before the declaration of posse. The oath is never a start or a holder date (the start rests on the declaration and the termo); no clock time is stored for it.

claims.text: After the oath, the President of Congress declared Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested ('Declaro empossados') as President and Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Nelson Carneiro) - Declaro empossados, para o período de 15 de março de 1990 a 1º de janeiro de 1995, como Presidente e Vice-Presidente ...

claims.uncertainty: Posse record with an explicit period beginning 15 March 1990: the basis for Itamar Franco's from as Vice-President. The printed period end (1 January 1995) is prospective and never an until. The President's posse in the same declaration is br_collor_posse_declared_congress_19900315.

claims.text: The termo de posse read by the First Secretary and signed at the session records that at 10:00 on 15 March 1990, before the National Congress in joint session in the Chamber's plenary, Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco were solemnly invested under Article 78 of the Constitution in the offices of President and Vice-President of the Republic, respectively, for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995, and took the prescribed oath.

locator.item: Termo de posse dos Excelentíssimos senhores Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello e Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, nos cargos, respectivamente, de Presidente e Vice-Presidente da República

claims.uncertainty: Signed termo of the same posse; supports the declaration. The termo's clock time (10:00) is not relied on (the minutes show the session reopening at 9:46).

claims.text: The same termo recites that the two had been elected in the second round on 17 December of the previous year and certified ('diplomados') by the Superior Electoral Court on 30 December of that year.

locator.item: Termo de posse: 'diplomados, pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, a trinta de dezembro do mesmo ano'

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital of the TSE act; agrees with the TSE diploma (br_itamar_vp_tse_diploma_issued_19891230). Never a holder date.

claims.uncertainty: The letter is a handwritten facsimile; the reading matches the typeset text in DCN Seção II of 31 December 1992.

claims.text: Immediately after the reading of Collor's letter, the President of Congress ordered its immediate publication in a special edition of the Diário do Congresso Nacional and declared the office of President of the Republic vacant, convening a solemn session for 12:30 that day for the Vice-President's oath; the session rose at 11:50.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Mauro Benevides) - ... declaro vago o cargo de Presidente da República

claims.uncertainty: Declaration of vacancy by the President of Congress; together with the letter and the termo below it supports Collor's until.

claims.text: At the solemn 3rd joint session of 29 December 1992 (opened at 12:30), after Itamar Franco took the constitutional oath, the President of Congress declared Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested ('empossado') as President of the Federative Republic of Brazil for the period 29 December 1992 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Mauro Benevides) - Declaro, com profunda emoção, empossado ...

claims.uncertainty: Posse record with an explicit mandate start of 29 December 1992 (the basis for Itamar Franco's from). The printed end of the period is prospective and is not used.

claims.text: The termo de posse records that at 12:30 on 29 December 1992, before the National Congress in joint session, Vice-President Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, elected in the second round of 17 December 1989, appeared to be invested under Article 79 of the Constitution in the office of President of the Republic by virtue of the resignation of Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello 'ocorrida nesta data' (which occurred on that date), and took the oath under Article 78.

locator.item: Termo de posse do Exmº Sr. Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco

claims.uncertainty: Signed termo of the same posse; its statement that the resignation occurred that day is also recorded as a separate claim for Collor.

claims.text: The same termo states that the office was filled by virtue of Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello's resignation, which occurred on 29 December 1992.

locator.item: Termo de posse, 'em virtude da renúncia ... ocorrida nesta data'

claims.uncertainty: States the day of the resignation, not a clock time. The letter was presented to the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 (br_collor_resignation_letter_read_senate_19921229) and read in Congress between 11:30 and 11:50; no source states the hour it took effect.

claims.text: Itamar Franco's handwritten declaration to the President of Congress, dated Brasília 29 December 1992 and published in the minutes, states that his declaration of assets that day is the same one he presented on 2 October of that year, when he assumed, as Vice-President, the exercise of the office of President of the Republic.

locator.item: É a seguinte a declaração recebida (handwritten)

claims.uncertainty: Retrospective statement by the Vice-President himself, handwritten; the reading 'em dia 2 de outubro do corrente ano, quando assumi a condição de Vice-Presidente em exercício do cargo de Presidente da República' was made from renders and confirmed by the independent check. Vice-President's exercise: claim only, never a holder or a start.

claims.text: At the 2nd joint session of 29 December 1992 (11:30-11:50), after Collor's letter was read and the office of President declared vacant, the President of Congress, Senator Mauro Benevides, said that in consequence he would inform the Vice-President of the Republic, Dr. Itamar Franco, that he must appear before Congress at 12:30 that day to take the oath as President of the Republic.

locator.item: 'Em conseqüência da vacância agora proclamada, irei cientificar o Vice-Presidente da República, Dr. Itamar Franco, de que deve comparecer hoje ao Congresso Nacional, às 12h30min'

claims.uncertainty: The President of Congress announces that he will notify the Vice-President ('irei cientificar'); the notification itself is not recorded in the issue. It styles Itamar Franco as Vice-President on 29 December 1992, before his posse as President. The vacancy it follows is that of the office of President (CLAUDE-C01-10's br_presidency_vacancy_declared_19921229, which is not cited on this role); it says nothing of the office of Vice-President, sets no end and states no vacancy of the Vice-Presidency.

claims.text: The termo de posse records that at 12:30 on 29 December 1992 Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, Vice-President of the Republic, elected in the second round on 17 December 1989, appeared before the National Congress in joint session to be invested, under Article 79 of the Constitution, in the office of President of the Republic by virtue of the resignation of Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello that day, and took the oath under Article 78.

locator.item: Termo de posse do Exmo Sr. Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco no cargo de Presidente da República: 'compareceu o Sr. Dr. Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, Vice-Presidente da República ... a fim de ser investido, de acordo com o art. 79 ...'

claims.uncertainty: The Vice-President's succession to the Presidency (his posse as President is CLAUDE-C01-10's br_itamar_posse_declared_congress_19921229 and br_itamar_termo_de_posse_19921229 on br_president). The record neither declares the office of Vice-President vacant nor states that his vice-presidential office ended, so it sets no until and no vacancy on br_vice_president; his posse as President is never an end of his vice-presidential office, and nothing is inferred from it.

locator.item: RESOLUÇÃO Nº 101, DE 1992, arts. 1-4 and dating line

claims.text: At the Senate's session as a court on 29 December 1992 (opened at 9:00), defence counsel José Moura Rocha said he had just spoken by telephone with the suspended President Fernando Collor de Mello and read to the Senate Collor's letter to the President of the National Congress, dated Brasília 29 December 1992 and signed 'F. Collor', stating that on that date and by that instrument he resigns the mandate of President of the Republic. The President of Congress, Mauro Benevides, then convened a joint session for 11:30 that day, and Minister Sydney Sanches suspended the Senate session at 9:43 so that Congress could receive the resignation and declare the vacancy; it reopened at 13:40.

locator.item: attendance at 9:00 (p. 2729); Moura Rocha's reading of the letter, with its handwritten facsimile (p. 2738); Benevides's convocation (p. 2741); 'Suspensa às 9h43min, a sessão é reaberta às 13h40min' (p. 2742)

claims.uncertainty: Places the letter's presentation to the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 on 29 December; the letter itself states the day, not a time. Congress read it and declared the vacancy between 11:30 and 11:50 (br_collor_resignation_letter_read_congress_19921229). Supports Collor's end, which stays day-only. Located by the independent check.

claims.text: When the session resumed, the Senate voted on whether the process should continue after the resignation: the panel printout headed '29.12.92 18:17 HORAS', 'PROSSEGUIMENTO DO PROCESSO DE IMPEACHMENT', shows 71 yes and 8 no; Sanches declared that the Senate had decided by 71 votes to 8 that the process against Collor should continue to consider the sanction of disqualification ('inabilitação'), and after two senators declared votes not registered on the panel he proclaimed 73 yes and 8 no.

locator.item: vote panel '29.12.92 18:17 HORAS 2.SESSAO 1.VOTACAO'; the proclamations by Sydney Sanches

claims.uncertainty: A procedural vote after the resignation; it concerns only the disqualification sanction and neither ends nor extends Collor's term. The panel prints 79 votes; the proclaimed total of 81 includes the two declared votes. Located by the independent check.

claims.text: The panel printout headed '30.12.92 04:21 HORAS', 'INABILITACAO POR OITO ANOS', records 76 yes, 3 no and no abstentions (total 79); Sanches announced the result, noting that abstention was not permitted, and read the sentence against Collor. The session rose at 4:40 on the following day, 30 December 1992.

locator.item: vote panel '30.12.92 04:21 HORAS 2.SESSAO 2.VOTACAO'; announcement of the result; closing line on PDF page 324 'Levanta-se a sessão às 4h40min do dia imediato'

claims.uncertainty: The vote on the eight-year disqualification ('inabilitação ... para o exercício de função pública'); it is not a loss of political rights and does not bound Collor's term, which ended with the resignation on 29 December. Located by the independent check.

claims.text: The Senate's filed copy of a Mandado de Notificação addressed to 'MICHEL TEMER, Vice-Presidente da República Federativa do Brasil', dated 'Senado Federal, em 12 de maio de 2016' and signed by Senator Renan Calheiros as President of the Senate, informs him that, the Chamber having authorized the process and the Senate having admitted it at its extraordinary session of 11 May 2016, President Dilma Vana Rousseff was intimated of Denúncia nº 1 of 2016; that from her receipt of the intimation the impeachment process is instituted and she is suspended from her functions under art. 86, § 1, II of the Constitution until the judgment ends or the 180-day period elapses; and that he is therefore to assume the Presidency immediately and on an interim basis ('assumir imediata e interinamente a Presidência da República') under art. 79.

locator.item: addressee block; paragraphs 1-2; dateline and signatures

claims.uncertainty: The notification instructs the Vice-President to assume on an interim basis; it does not record the hour, or that he did so. Interim exercise of the Presidency is a claim only: it never makes him a holder of br_president, and it neither ends nor splits his br_vice_president holder.

roles.title: President of the Federative Republic of Brazil

holder_claims.name: José Sarney
holder_claims.note: Observed on 5 January 1990, signing Decree No. 98.797 as President (the Presidency's archived legislation page): the earliest 1990 attestation pinned to a byte-stable response. He also signed Decree No. 99.167 on 13 March 1990; that act is a claim on the role, not a holder date.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: his 1985 assumption lies outside the packet period. No end: no primary source reviewed states the day his term ended; the Presidency Library's retrospective span (15.03.1985-15.03.1990) is a claim only, the Constitution's transitional provision is procedure only, and Collor's posse of 15 March 1990 is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Fernando Collor de Mello
holder_claims.note: From 15 March 1990: the President of Congress declared him invested for the period beginning that day, and the termo records the posse at 10:00 (DCN nº 8/1990); in his address he says he has just assumed the Presidency. Until 29 December 1992: his letter resigns the mandate 'nesta data e por este instrumento', the President of Congress declared the office vacant that day, and Itamar Franco's termo de posse states that the resignation occurred that day; the letter was also read to the Senate that morning.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is day-only: the letter reached the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 and was read in Congress between 11:30 and 11:50, and no source states the hour of effect. He was suspended from 2 October 1992 on receiving the summons (a claim); the suspension is not an end and the holder is not split. The TSE diploma (30 December 1989) and the ballots of 15 November and 17 December 1989 are separate claims. The judgment of 30 December 1992 and Resolução nº 101 (disqualification for eight years) follow the resignation and bound nothing.

holder_claims.name: Itamar Franco

roles.scope_note: President of the Federative Republic of Brazil under the 1988 Constitution, recorded here as head of state (the office is also head of government). CLAUDE-C01-10 keeps popular election, diplomação by the Superior Electoral Court, the oath before Congress, the declaration of posse, the termo de posse, assumption statements, sash ceremonies, the Chamber's authorization, the Senate's admission, the summons and its receipt (suspension), the Vice-President's exercise of the office, resignation, vacancy, the Senate's judgment, removal and disqualification as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a declaration of posse or a termo de posse states that the person was invested for a period beginning that day, and an end only where a source states the day a resignation or removal took effect; otherwise it is dated by attested_on. Oaths, elections, diplomações and sash ceremonies are never boundaries; periods declared at a posse are prospective and never ends; a successor's or third party's statement that the predecessor leaves office is a claim only; retrospective Presidency Library spans are claims with no structured date. A Vice-President exercising the office (Itamar Franco in 1992, Michel Temer in 2016, Hamilton Mourão in 2022) is recorded as claims, never as a holder of it. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. Vice-presidents, ministers and party offices are otherwise outside this role.

roles.scope_note: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil under the 1988 Constitution, recorded as an institutional office of the Presidency (the 1985 claims of BR-VP-01 are pre-period context under the earlier Constitution). CLAUDE-C01-17 keeps popular election, diplomação by the Superior Electoral Court, the oath before Congress, the declaration of posse, the termo de posse, same-session styling, styling of the incumbent before a new posse, the Vice-President's notification to exercise and exercise of the Presidency as substitute or on an interim basis, the Vice-President's succession to the Presidency, any vacancy and any stated end as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a declaration of posse or a termo de posse states that the person was invested as Vice-President for a period beginning that day, and an end only where a source states the day the vice-presidential office ended; otherwise it is dated by attested_on. No reviewed primary source states such an end or a vacancy of the Vice-Presidency, so no holder has an end and no vacancy is recorded: a successor's posse, the Vice-President's posse as President (1992, 2016), the vacancy of the office of President and periods declared at a posse are never ends. A Vice-President exercising the Presidency is recorded as claims, never as a holder of br_president or of this role, and the exercise neither splits nor ends a holder. Elections, diplomações, oaths, styling of the incumbent and a successor's tribute are never boundaries; retrospective Vice-Presidency and Presidency Library spans and chronologies are claims with no structured date. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. Twelve claims recorded by CLAUDE-C01-10 (the 1989 diplomação ceremony, the Vice-President's notification and exercise of the Presidency in 1992, 2016 and 2022 and a Presidency Library span) keep their br_president rows and are cited here; CLAUDE-C01-10's Rádio Senado news item is a lead for this role and is not cited, the notification resting on the Senate's case file (volume 48) and matter page; this role's own rows carry role_id br_vice_president. Ministers and party offices are outside this role.

unresolved: Presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-10, BR-PRES-01..10) are dated holder observations from primary Congress, Senate, Chamber, Presidency and electoral-court records. Still open: a primary record of the day José Sarney's term ended (only the Presidency Library's retrospective span gives 15 March 1990); the TSE's own minutes of the 1989-2022 diplomações; and the Diário Oficial da União originals, whose viewer requires a CAPTCHA.

Stated starts: every posse from 15 March 1990 to 1 January 2023. Stated ends: Fernando Collor de Mello (resignation, 29 December 1992) and Dilma Rousseff (Resolution No. 35, 31 August 2016) only. The ends of Itamar Franco, of each first term, of Cardoso's and Lula's second terms, of Temer and of Bolsonaro are not stated by an event record; periods declared at a posse, successors' statements, a successor's posse and 'ex-Presidente' styling are not used as ends.

Clock times: no source states the hour Collor's resignation took effect (the letter reached the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 and was read in Congress between 11:30 and 11:50 on 29 December 1992) or the hour Rousseff received the intimation on 12 May 2016. Termo clock times differ from the session openings and are not used.

Sash transfers: only the 1 January 2019 ceremony has a Presidency record, with a misprinted dateline and no named giver; none was found for 1990, 1995, 2003, 2011, 2015 or 2023 (Senate and Chamber news-agency reports of 2003 and 2011 are leads). The Vice-President's exercise of the office (Itamar Franco from 2 October 1992, Michel Temer from 12 May 2016, Hamilton Mourão on 30-31 December 2022) is recorded only as claims.

Vice-Presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-17, BR-VP-01..10): the second role, br_vice_president, holds nine holder observations, each starting on a stated posse (Itamar Franco 15 March 1990; Marco Maciel 1995 and 1999; José Alencar 2003 and 2007; Michel Temer 2011 and 2015; Hamilton Mourão 2019; Geraldo Alckmin 2023). No reviewed primary source states the end of any vice-presidential term or a vacancy of the Vice-Presidency: not on 1 January 1990, not after Itamar Franco's posse as President on 29 December 1992 and not after Temer's on 31 August 2016 (the vacancies declared on those days are of the Presidency). Retrospective spans and the Vice-Presidency's chronology are claims only.

Still open for the Vice-Presidency: a contemporaneous record of the office on 1 January 1990 (vacant or held); the day each term ended; the hour Michel Temer began exercising the Presidency on 12 May 2016; the Vice-Presidency's own pages on gov.br (bot-check pages, not bypassed), the Diário Oficial da União (CAPTCHA) and the TSE's diplomação minutes. The Vice-President's exercise of the Presidency (1985, 1991, 1992, 2016, 2022 and 2026) is recorded only as claims.
